subject: Private endpoint egress allowlist + DNS behavior — request for SLA exception
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@healthcorp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Ops Team <ops@healthcorp.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private endpoint egress / DNS behavior question + SLA exception request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're starting to map our firewall and NAT rules for the Redwood private endpoint (VPC peering + on-prem runtime) and have a couple of asks before procurement signs off:

1) Canonical allowlist: can you provide a minimal set of IPs (or stable prefixes) that the control plane and runtime will originate connections from for the next 12 months? Our security team prefers IPs over FQDNs.
2) DNS / split-horizon: If we keep split-horizon DNS internally (so the private endpoint resolves internally), will anything still need to egress to public FQDNs for telemetry, model updates, or license checks? If so, list ports/FQDNs and whether mTLS/SNI is used.
3) Ephemeral rotation: do you rotate egress addresses frequently? If yes, what is the rotation cadence and how will you notify us?
4) SLA exception: we need a temporary SLA variance for the private control plane (change from 99.95 to 99.9) tied to our legacy on-prem gateway constraints. Can Redwood provide a one-quarter exception while we finish the gateway refresh?

I've attached our current SG export (healthcorp_sg_rules.xlsx) to illustrate our starting point. Procurement will want the allowlist and a DocuSign reference to include in the contract.

Appreciate a consolidated reply that we can share with security and procurement.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Cloud Engineering | HealthCorp Inc.
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@healthcorp.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress / DNS behavior question + SLA exception request

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. I copied infra and ops for runbook/ops confirmations. Below is a consolidated answer and a proposal for the allowlist approach.

Short answers (summary):
- Control plane egress: three stable /28s (listed below) for control-plane telemetry, heartbeat and provisioning. We can provide IPs or a short CSV (redwood-egress-ips-v1.csv attached).
- Runtime/model fetch: only used during image/model sync windows; those originate from the same IP pool but are callable from our internal subnets — you can restrict to the same prefixes.
- Telemetry/metrics: outbound TLS to telemetry.redwood.ai on 443. We use SNI and expect customers to allow the FQDN or the IPs; we do not depend on DNS fallback to public internet when private endpoint is used, except for automated vulnerability feeds (see note).
- Rotation: ephemeral rotation for a small subset of addresses (for scale) on a weekly cadence; the three primary /28s are stable for 12+ months. We'll publish rotation notices to the Ops runbook URL and provide a signed CSV in DocuSign when/if rotation affects you.

Proposed allowlist (minimal):
- Control plane (stable): 52.34.120.0/28, 52.34.121.0/28, 52.34.122.0/28
- Optional telemetry FQDN: telemetry.redwood.ai (443, TLS w/SNI) — if you cannot allow FQDNs, allow 52.34.130.15 and 52.34.130.16 (note: these may be part of ephemeral pool).
- Health-check / NAT poke: 52.34.140.10 (TCP/443) — used for LL runtime health pings from our control plane.

Mapping to your questions: 
1) Yes — see CSV attached. We'll include a signed artifact for procurement.
2) Split-horizon: you do not need outbound access to model registry FQDNs if the private endpoint is resolving internally; however, we recommend outbound to telemetry.redwood.ai for metrics unless you forward metrics via your telemetry collector.
3) Rotation cadence: weekly for ephemeral addresses; primary /28s are stable.
4) SLA exception: we can provision a 90-day temporary SLA variance (99.9) with contract language. Legal will need a DocuSign acknowledgement; procurement and I should loop in legal to sign the limited variance.

Next steps:
- David: can you confirm the runbook steps and the ops notification flow for rotation?
- Marcus: can you confirm whether TLS fingerprinting (JA3 hash) is available as an acceptance artifact?
- Sanjay / procurement: confirm whether IP CSV is sufficient for signatures or if you require a notarized Excel with signatures.

Attachments: redwood-egress-ips-v1.csv (proposed), referenced in metadata.

Thanks,
— Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress / DNS behavior question + SLA exception request

Kim — quick ops confirmation and a couple implementation notes.

1) Runbook & notification: We'll add a rotation notification webhook and a short bulletin to https://drive.redwood.com/egress-runbook/allowlist-onprem.md. Notifications: weekly digest for ephemeral rotations + ad-hoc pager for any forced reassignments.
2) JA3 / TLS fingerprint: we do not publish JA3 as a stable artifact (it can change with OpenSSL upgrades). Instead we can provide:
   - TLS server certificate chain (PEM) that our control plane presents for mutual endpoints, and
   - SNI hostnames we use (telemetry.redwood.ai, control.redwood.ai).
3) Operational tasks for HealthCorp:
   - Create the three /28 routes in your perimeter NAT with a static mapping to the private endpoint egress SNAT pool.
   - Allow outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood.ai (or the two optional IPs if you prefer).
   - Allow inbound health-check return flows for 52.34.140.10 (we will only initiate TCP from control-plane).
4) Evidence pack: we can produce an attestation PDF showing IP ownership and a signed CSV; Ops will draft the attestation and post to the DocuSign link once Legal signs off.

I approve the minimal allowlist above as Ops owner — implementation wise we will:
- Hold at least 14 days notice for scheduled rotations that affect your assigned stable IPs.
- If forced reassignments happen, we will open an incident with HealthCorp and provide mitigation guidance.

— David
David Kim
Director, Production Infra | Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@healthcorp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthcorp.com, Ops Team <ops@healthcorp.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress / DNS behavior question + SLA exception request

Kim / team — this is helpful, thank you. Procurement wants the signed allowlist CSV and the 90-day SLA variance language captured in DocuSign (we'll circulate on our side). Two clarifications before we proceed: 

- Is the 52.34.140.10 health-check IP consistent across regions? We have separate firewall clusters east/west and need to ensure the address is the same.
- For telemetry: we prefer FQDN exceptions rather than IPs. Please ensure the attestation includes the telemetry.redwood.ai CNAME chain and certificate thumbprint so our security team can match TLS.

If those two items are addressed, procurement will attach the CSV and the signed SLA variance to the PO and we can schedule an implementation window the following week.

I'll loop Legal on the DocuSign thread after procurement sends an initial envelope.

— Sanjay
